description: An interactive field guide to Mercury: why orbiting the innermost planet costs more than leaving the Solar System, Mariner 10 and Giuseppe Colombo's gravity-assist idea, MESSENGER's six flybys and 0.86 km/s capture in 2011, its ceramic sunshade, the 3:2 spin–orbit resonance that makes a Mercury day last 176 Earth days, polar ice, and ESA–JAXA's BepiColombo, due to enter orbit on 21 November 2026.
og: 13.9 km/s to orbit Mercury, a sunshade at 370 °C, and a day two years long: MESSENGER and BepiColombo, interactive and sourced from NASA, APL and ESA.
brand: SCORCH — TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDE / ТЕХНИЧЕСКИЙ СПРАВОЧНИК
